findings.desc: experiments/role-prompt-ab-replay/lib/replay.mjs:301-305 and protocol.json:14-23 — The two A/B arms are not pinned legacy/modular role-prompt bytes or a verified prompt-envelope reconstruction; armPrompt synthesizes one short label sentence per arm. `node experiments/role-prompt-ab-replay/run.mjs --json` therefore reports 1279 vs 1292 bytes for critical-01, measuring the labels plus shared JSON rather than either real role contract. This can validate harness determinism but cannot constitute a role-prompt A/B assembled-input measurement. Bind each arm to exact committed prompt/envelope bytes plus digest/contract version, or classify the arm metric itself INCONCLUSIVE and rename the artifact as a framework selfcheck.

experiments/role-prompt-ab-replay/corpus.json:81-83,123-125,165-167,207-209 and lib/replay.mjs:308-320 — finding recall is marked EVALUABLE solely by replaying caller-authored `observedFindingsByArm`; those arm observations carry no source artifact, transcript/reviewer-run reference, evidence digest, or independent adjudication binding. The oracle `adjudication.evidenceRef` only supports that the seeded defect is valid, not that arm A or B actually detected it. `selfcheck.mjs` then prints `Recall: EVALUABLE` while merely checking schema/digests. Treat unbound arm outcomes exactly like unbound provider usage: reject numeric/detected observations or return INCONCLUSIVE until every arm observation is mechanically bound to immutable review output and independently adjudicated matching evidence.
